newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico energy projects seen helping economy.
newsitem.headline: Mexico energy projects seen helping economy.

text.p: Two large projects undertaken by state-owned Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) will help restart growth in the Mexican economy, the Energy Ministery said in a statement.
It said that the modernization of the Cantarell complex, locaed in the Sonda de Campeche, will cost $825 million in 1997.
It now produces 1.1 million barrels of oil a day. The project aims to increase production of crude oil by an average of 150,000 barrels a day and eliminate the burning of natural gas.
The Ministry said that an investment of $1.2 billion will overhaul the Cadereyta refinery, located near Monterrey.
The work will include the construction of 10 plants, the expansion of six and the modernization of six more.
"Both projects will aid the recuperation of the national economy...," the Ministry said.
